parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime: no trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police, border or facility targeting of trans visitors, and no documented facility exclusion, marker-based custody or screening. Sodomy law was decriminalised in December 2022, though the status of a former 16+ 'serious indecency' provision is unresolved. Exposures: official and religious hostility rhetoric; one violent attack on a trans activist (2018) with a nominal sentence and no jail time, the only documented incident and dated; employment protection omits gender identity (resident-facing). Protections: civil society operates (Pride events, vigils, activism) and a visa rule was changed to admit same-sex spouses. Border, care, custody and minors are not documented, so uncertainty is real. No trans-specific violence rate exists, so the violence axis is thinly documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented for trans visitors; no marker-mismatch screening or refusal recorded.
entry_documents.protection: Remote-work visa entry rules were amended to admit same-sex spouses (sexuality, not trans-specific).
entry_documents.interaction: Home-passport markers would govern entry; no record of how foreign documents are treated.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented detention or custody of trans visitors; no documented birth-sex placement.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented trans-specific criminal offence in force.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody practice unknown, so placement risk cannot be assessed.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented; the dossier describes one island-wide regime with no facility rules recorded.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No facility exclusion or bathroom restriction recorded.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence is not treated as safety; facility access is unverified.

care_services.exposure: No transition-healthcare findings; denial or refusal to trans visitors is undocumented.
care_services.protection: Fertility centre serves lesbian couples only (not trans-specific).
care_services.interaction: No documented emergency-care or ward-placement practice for trans patients.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government and religious rhetoric frames LGBT people as external imposition; justice department refused legal change; fundamentalist groups argue discrimination should be encouraged (tier 3 social hostility at most).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Prime minister reported as pro-LGBT; Catholic church and a bishop reported as respecting LGBT rights.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official rhetoric is hostile but no documented state action against trans travellers.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for trans minors; former serious-indecency provision (16+) status unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minors travelling with guardians have no documented custody or school exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One documented 2018 cleaver attack on a trans activist; sentence of a fine or three months with no jail time (impunity outcome, dated, single incident; no trans-specific rate).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Conviction obtained; public reporting and advocacy follow-up occurred.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Weak sentencing shows limited deterrence; no later incident is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Regional commission case status after decriminalisation unresolved; employment exclusion of gender identity documented as a barrier for trans residents.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional challenge succeeded; sodomy statute struck down in 2022/2023 rulings; civil-society events held in the capital.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist, but recourse for trans people specifically (hate-crime or gender-identity protection) is not documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier on exposure: 0.55-B has documented border secondary screening and refused admission, which this dossier does not record, so this case sits higher on border risk. It is similar in showing weak remedies and discretionary harm with no documented criminal exposure.
This case is higher: 0.55-E documents recurring ejection, selective scrutiny and harassment by state-authorised actors, while this dossier documents only rhetoric and one dated attack.

This case is lower: 0.65-C documents working remedies (injunction, damages, fines on the perpetrator) and a recent appellate ruling enforced for a visitor. This dossier shows a nominal sentence and no equivalent recourse for trans people.
This case is higher: 0.45-B documents state-mandated exclusion from schools and clinics for visitors, which is absent here.

parsed.synthesis: The known exposures are social and rhetorical: official and religious hostility, one violent attack resolved with a nominal sentence, and employment exclusion for trans residents. No trans-specific criminal offence, state targeting, facility exclusion or documented custody harm applies to visitors. Civil society operates visibly, and decriminalisation shows institutional movement, though recourse for trans people is not documented. Key border, care, custody and minor-exposure questions remain unanswered, so they are treated as open rather than as safety. The rating sits in the elevated-to-reduced boundary because documented impunity and hostile official rhetoric offset the absence of state-directed exposure.
